Drive Medical Deluxe Walker Review | Canes&Walkers.com

# Drive Medical Deluxe Walker Review

 

Most people think that walkers like the Deluxe Two Button Folding Walker with 5-Inch Wheels are only useful to the elderly who reside in a nursing facility. That isn’t the case at all! A device like this one can be a great help to anyone with mobility issues due to an illness, an injury, or a developmental condition!

In this review, we are going to talk a little more about the features of the Deluxe Two Button Folding Walker with 5-Inch Wheels, but we are also going to give you an overview of what people who have purchased the walker had to say about their overall experience with it.

Then, we’re going to give you our recommendation on whether or not this walker with wheels is something you should consider purchasing for your own loved ones—or yourself!

## About The Product

When crutches won’t do because you need more support to keep yourself balanced, the Deluxe Two Button Folding Walker with 5-Inch Wheels will be able to provide you with that, and more. From the moment you put your hands on the ergonomic vinyl hand grips, you can expect that you’ll be able to get around just a little bit easier, but also more comfortably.

### Notable Features Of The Product

- Comes with wheels and a vinyl contoured hand grip
- Each side operates independently to allow easy movement
- Easy push-button mechanisms may be operated by fingers, palms or side of hand
- Newly designed rear glide cap allows for walker to slide easily and smoothly over most surfaces
- Sturdy 1 inch diameter aluminum construction ensures maximum strength

What makes this walker special is that each side operates independently from the other. This means that you’ll be able to navigate tight spaces with ease.

 The walker features a push button mechanism that allows the device to fold up neatly and compactly, making it the perfect solution for those who are short on space, or who need to put their walker in the car while traveling.

The U-Shaped design on the lightweight frame allows you more space to walk without making yourself feel claustrophobic. The aluminum walker also features a cross-frame design that gives the device and you more stability.

That stability will allow you to feel more confident while walking. Also, for ease of use, the walker features two 5 inch wheels and rear glide caps that will make it possible for you to traverse different types of surfaces with ease.

## What People Had To Say

When looking at what people had to say about the Deluxe Two Button Folding Walker with 5-Inch Wheels, the majority of customers raved about this particular walker. The thing people liked the most about this walker was how easy it was to put the unit together, but also how to adjust the height of the legs.

Some customers did say that the walker was too large, as the wheels are on the outside of the walker. You can make the walker a little more narrow by switching the front legs so that the wheels are inside. It’s a simple fix that takes no time at all to do.

Some other things customers like was how easily the wheels (and the rear grips) are able to glide on a variety of surfaces. Folks said that they were able to go from hard flooring to carpeting without any problems. People also liked that the hand grips were cushioned, but they also liked that this walker is easy to collapse and assemble when they are traveling.

While many people enjoyed their walker, there were some who were not as satisfied with their purchase. These customers were disappointed by how unstable their walker felt.

Some said that when they walked with it, it would wobble, shake, and they stopped using it because of how unstable the walker felt. Other customers said the wheels of their walker squeaked, even when using lubricant.

Another complaint people had was that the walker was hard to put together. They found that once the walker was put together, the unit would fold down flat and it took up more room than they would have liked.

Also, because these customers had some concerns and wanted to return the product, they were very upset that they were not able to return the product.

## Our Recommendation

Searching for a walker that is going to be sturdy enough for you to comfortably and confidently walk when you already have mobility and balance problems can be stressful—especially when there are so many options out there on the market. The Deluxe Two Button Folding Walker with 5-Inch Wheels is a walker that is designed to remedy that problem.

This particular walker is designed to be easy to assemble and disassemble. The individual locking mechanism on either side of the walker allows you to fold the walker for easy storage when the device isn’t being used or if it needs to be stored in the trunk of a car.

We like this walker because it is an affordable walker that will help you regain your mobility. The wheels and the rear glide caps gives you the opportunity to move from surface to surface with little to no effort or strain on your behalf. The contoured vinyl grip is going to fit comfortably in your hand so your hands don’t cramp or ache while using the walker.

Whether you are recovering from an injury, an illness, or if you are an elderly individual who has having trouble getting around, we believe that the Deluxe Two Button Folding Walker with 5-Inch Wheels is a terrific (and affordable) option. It’s a lightweight walker that isn’t going to require much strength to lift, allowing you to focus on walking safely.

results.title: Best walkers for seniors: 9 models tested by Consumer Reports
results.author: Anthony Lopopolo
results.text:
Best walkers for seniors: 9 models tested by Consumer Reports

# The best walkers for seniors, as tested by Consumer Reports

A mobility aid that's hard to control often goes unused. Consumer Reports tested nine walkers on handling, weight, and folding ease to find the best

By Anthony Lopopolo

· Updated June 12, 2026

Mobio Marketing / Unsplash

Seniors dealing with balance issues, neuropathy, or recovery from surgery rely on walkers to stay mobile and independent. Weight, wheel design, and folding mechanisms affect daily usability in ways that aren't obvious from a product listing. A walker that's difficult to control or hard to lift in and out of a car can quickly go unused.

Consumer Reports had a tester with firsthand balance challenges try all nine walkers on carpet, hard floors, concrete, and uneven outdoor surfaces to find the best options for seniors.

## Drive Medical Trigger Release Folding Walker

Credit: Amazon

The Drive Medical Trigger Release costs $47.91, weighs 7 pounds, and has a 350-pound weight limit. Consumer Reports named it the top pick overall after the tester found it moved more smoothly on carpets and hard floors than any other model in the test. CR noted the trigger-fold mechanism was far easier to operate than the push-button systems on other walkers, allowing the user to fold it without removing hands from the handles and risking a loss of balance.

## Drive Medical Two Button Folding Walker with Wheels

Credit: Amazon

This walker costs $27.69, weighs 7.2 pounds, and supports users up to 350 pounds. Consumer Reports highlighted its dual adjustability in both height and width as the standout feature, noting it was the only model tested with width adjustment. CR found the permanent glide caps on the back legs allowed smooth transitions from carpet to tile without snagging, a practical advantage for home use on mixed flooring.

## Walgreens Folding Walker with Wheels

Credit: Consumer Reports

At $69.99, the Walgreens $WBA model weighs 6.3 pounds and supports users up to 300 pounds. Consumer Reports found assembly straightforward, noting the walker unfolds and clicks into place out of the box. The tester noted a significant control problem, however. CR reported that the front wheels turned inward while walking, making the walker hard to direct and requiring constant concentration to use.

## Medical King Lightweight Walker with Wheels

The Medical King model is priced at $39.99, weighs 8.8 pounds, and supports users up to 350 pounds. Consumer Reports noted that most walkers only adjust for height, making this model's dual height-and-width adjustability a notable feature for users with a wider frame. CR found it easy to use, with front wheels and rubber-tipped back legs, and noted that switching the back legs to gliders would be a simple modification.

## Medline Two Button Folding Walker with Wheels

Credit: Amazon

This Medline model starts at $36, weighs 8 pounds, and has a 300-pound weight capacity. Consumer Reports found it moved smoothly over carpet and flat outdoor surfaces, with 5-inch front wheels and rubber caps on the back legs. CR noted the hard rubber handles were comfortable for short distances and easy to clean, but suggested adding soft covers for extended use.

Pepe Mobility Walking Frame with Wheels

Priced at $100, this 7.7-pound walker has a weight limit of 220 pounds. Consumer Reports found it outperformed all other walkers on uneven surfaces like gravel and grass. CR cautioned that the pressure-brake system requires users to hold the handles up to keep the back feet off the ground. Letting the handles drop causes the back legs to catch and stop the walker abruptly.

Carex Folding Standup Walker

Weighing 6.6 pounds and priced at $43.40, this wheel-free model supports users up to 300 pounds. Consumer Reports identified it as the right choice for users who need maximum stability, noting it requires the user to lift the walker fully off the ground with each step. CR described the aluminum construction as extremely lightweight, making it manageable for one person to lift in and out of a vehicle.

Medline Two-Button Folding Walker without Wheels

Available for $34.49, this wheel-free model weighs just 5 pounds and supports users up to 300 pounds. Consumer Reports called it easy to pick up and transport, noting the detachable sides make storage and car trunk loading less cumbersome. CR found it provides reliable standing stability for users who lose their balance easily, and noted that wheels or gliders can be added separately if mobility needs change.

Equate Folding Walker

This 8.5-pound model is priced at $57 and supports users up to 350 pounds. Consumer Reports found the trigger-fold mechanism allowed one-handed folding and that the included leg extensions let users skip the wheels if needed. CR flagged one significant flaw in testing. The wheels sometimes locked up and failed to swivel, making turns difficult and potentially dangerous for users who regularly walk around corners.
